questions.question: When examining the actual record of democracies on being 'responsive to the needs and demands of the people', what does historical evidence suggest?
options: Democracies fulfill 100% of all citizen requests within 24 hours of petitioning
Democracies are immune to corruption and bribery at all bureaucratic tiers
Democracies never experience worker strikes or civic demonstrations
Democracies often frustrate the needs of the people and frequently ignore the demands of a majority of their population
questions.explanation: The record of democracies is not impressive on responsiveness: democracies often frustrate the needs of the people and often ignore the demands of a majority of its population. The routine tales of corruption are enough to convince that democracy is not free of this evil.

questions.question: Does non-democratic rule eliminate bureaucratic corruption better than democracy?
options: No; there is nothing to show that non-democracies are less corrupt or more sensitive to the people, but their corruption is concealed from public scrutiny
Yes; non-democratic rulers are constitutionally incapable of accepting bribes
Yes; military dictatorships execute all corrupt officials within one hour
No; non-democracies have no government officials or revenue systems
questions.explanation: There is nothing to show that non-democracies are less corrupt or more sensitive to the people. In fact, in dictatorships there is no free press or independent judiciary to investigate and expose corruption.

questions.question: If you want to evaluate democracies on the basis of expected institutional practices, which regular setup would you look for?
options: Single-party rule with life tenure for the prime minister
Regular, free and fair elections, open public debate on major policies and legislation, and citizens' right to information
Judicial appointments made directly by the army chief of staff
Mandatory government censorship on all private news media
questions.explanation: To measure democracy on expected outcomes, we look for practices and institutions: regular, free and fair elections; open public debate on major policies and legislations; and citizens' right to information about the government and its functioning.

questions.subtopic: Record on Free and Fair Elections
questions.question: What does the historical record show regarding democracies holding regular and fair elections?
options: No democracy has ever managed to conduct more than one general election
Elections in all democracies are completely rigged by commercial corporations
Most democracies have succeeded in setting up regular and free elections, though fair elections offering every voter equal opportunity still face challenges
Democracies have replaced ballot voting with hereditary succession
questions.explanation: Most democracies have set up regular and free elections and conditions for open public debate. But most democracies fall short of elections that provide a fair chance to everyone and in subjecting every decision to public debate.

questions.subtopic: Inequality in Brazil and South Africa
questions.question: In highly unequal democratic countries such as South Africa and Brazil, official data indicates that:
options: National income is distributed with perfect mathematical equality to each citizen
The bottom 20% owns 95% of all national agricultural land and gold mines
Taxation has abolished the concept of private personal earnings
The top 20% of the population takes away more than 60% of the national income, while the bottom 20% receives less than 3%
questions.explanation: In countries like South Africa and Brazil, the top 20% people take away more than 60% of the national income, leaving less than 3% for the bottom 20%. This illustrates severe income inequality in electoral democracies.

questions.subtopic: Democracy as a Condition vs Outcome
questions.question: Political science clarifies that democracy is primarily a 'form of government'. What does this imply for solving socio-economic problems?
options: It can only create conditions for achieving something; the citizens have to take advantage of those conditions and achieve those goals
It automatically solves all poverty and unemployment without any citizen effort
It relieves citizens of any duty to pay taxes or obey traffic laws
It guarantees that all citizens will become millionaire investors
questions.explanation: Our first step is to recognise that democracy is just a form of government. It can only create conditions for achieving something. The citizens have to take advantage of those conditions and achieve those goals.

questions.question: Why did non-democratic regimes like Sri Lanka (historically under majoritarian policies) fail to accommodate diversity compared to power-sharing democracies like Belgium?
options: Sri Lanka had too many regional parliamentary elections every month
Belgium forced all citizens to speak a single newly invented language
Non-democratic and majoritarian systems often turn a blind eye to or suppress internal social differences, leading to violent civil strife
Sri Lanka banned foreign tourism and international tea exports
questions.explanation: The ability to handle social differences, divisions and conflict is a definite plus point of democratic regimes. But the example of Sri Lanka reminds us that a democracy must fulfill two conditions (working with minority, avoiding majoritarian oppression) to achieve this.

questions.question: Even though poor voters constitute a massive proportion of the electorate in democracies, why do democratically elected governments often seem reluctant to address poverty aggressively?
options: Because the constitution legally forbids spending revenue on welfare schemes
Because rich donors and powerful commercial lobbies exert immense influence over party campaigns and economic policy decisions
Because poor citizens are barred from voting in general elections
Because the United Nations disallows domestic antipoverty programs
questions.explanation: The poor constitute a large proportion of our voters and no party will like to lose their votes. Yet democratically elected governments do not appear to be as keen to address the question of poverty as you would expect them to, largely due to political complacency and influence of economic elites.

questions.question: Which of the following scenarios best demonstrates that people are acting as 'citizens' rather than 'subjects' in a democracy?
options: Citizens organise peaceful demonstrations and file public petitions demanding accountability when a bridge project fails safety audits
Citizens quietly obey every administrative edict without questioning misuse of funds
Citizens celebrate hereditary dynastic rulers with unconditional loyalty
Citizens refuse to participate in census surveys or register their births
questions.explanation: The transformation of people from the status of subjects to citizens occurs when they recognise their rights, critically assess ruler actions, and organise civic actions to hold officials accountable.

questions.question: Why is individual freedom and dignity inherently safer in a democracy than in a monarchy or military junta?
options: Because monarchs sign contracts with trade unions every morning
Because military generals are forbidden from commanding soldiers
Because autocracies have no police forces or jails
Because democratic constitutions grant fundamental civil rights enforceable by an independent judiciary
questions.explanation: Democracy stands much superior to any other form of government in promoting dignity and freedom of the individual. In non-democracies, the principle of individual freedom often has no legal or moral backing, and subjects cannot demand rights as legal entitlements.

questions.question: If a democratic system permanently excludes a minority community from ever participating in the ruling majority coalition based purely on their birth or religion, what happens to that democracy?
options: The democracy automatically becomes the wealthiest economy on Earth
The country qualifies for automatic permanent membership in the UN Security Council
Democracy ceases to be accommodative for that group and violates the fundamental principle of democratic equality
The minority group achieves supreme legislative veto power
questions.explanation: Democracy remains democracy only as long as every citizen has a chance of being in majority at some point of time. If someone is barred from being in majority on the basis of birth, then the democratic rule ceases to be accommodative for that person or group.

questions.subtopic: Democracy and Economic Quality of Life
questions.question: When examining poor countries under democratic rule versus poor countries under authoritarian rule, what does empirical evidence demonstrate about human development?
options: Authoritarian poor countries have ten times higher literacy rates than any democracy
Democracies have higher infant mortality rates than any dictatorship
All authoritarian regimes achieve 100% university graduation rates
There is negligible difference in economic growth rates, but democracies offer vastly superior civil liberties and social security protection
questions.explanation: The difference in rates of economic growth between less developed countries with dictatorships and democracies is negligible. Overall, we cannot say that democracy is a guarantee of economic development, but we can expect democracy not to lag behind dictatorships in this respect while preserving human rights.

questions.question: Even if male chauvinism and domestic violence still persist in many households, why is the democratic recognition of women's rights a decisive turning point?
options: It provides women with legal rights and institutional standing to wage organized struggles against injustice in courts and public forums
It automatically converts all husbands into domestic servants
It bans men from entering legislative assemblies
It dissolves all family institutions permanently
questions.explanation: Once the principle of equal treatment of women is recognised, it becomes easier for women to wage a struggle against what is now unacceptable legally and morally. In a non-democratic setup, this unacceptability would not have legal basis.

questions.question: Why did multinational and multi-ethnic democracies like India remain united, while some authoritarian regimes collapsed into ethnic Balkanisation?

Because democratic power sharing and linguistic state reorganization accommodated regional aspirations within a unified constitutional framework
Because India maintained mandatory military rule across all state capitals

questions.subtopic: The Voice of the Ordinary Citizen
questions.question: In a democracy, what transforms an ordinary voter from a helpless subject into an empowered political sovereign?
options: Direct monetary subsidies deposited every night by commercial banks
The constitutional right to universal adult franchise, secret ballot, and regular accountability of rulers
The privilege of carrying military firearms in parliament
Exemption from all criminal and civil penal laws
questions.explanation: Universal adult franchise, equal voting power ('one person, one vote, one value'), and regular elections give every citizen a constitutional voice that politicians cannot ignore.

questions.subtopic: Expectations from Democracy as an Indicator
questions.question: When citizens express dissatisfaction that public hospitals and government schools are not functioning adequately, this demonstrates that:
options: Citizens have developed high democratic consciousness and hold the state accountable for public welfare delivery
Citizens want to replace democracy with a military dictatorship immediately
The country should permanently abolish public healthcare and education
Elections have failed completely and should be canceled
questions.explanation: The fact that people are complaining is itself a testimony to the success of democracy: it shows that people have developed awareness and the ability to expect and to look critically at power holders and the high and the mighty.

questions.question: Which of the following is an undeniable structural defect inherent in non-democratic regimes?
options: They spend too much time debating legislation in public assemblies
They are compelled to publish all financial transactions on public websites
They give supreme veto rights to independent trade unions

questions.question: Which statement best captures the realistic assessment of democratic outcomes according to the NCERT curriculum?
options: Democracy guarantees that every family will receive identical income regardless of effort
Democracy has proved worse than military rule in protecting fundamental human liberties
Democracy is not a magical cure for all ills, but it provides the most just, transparent, and dignified institutional framework for human self-governance
Democracy functions perfectly without any citizen participation or vigilance
questions.explanation: Democracy is not a magical solution to all economic and social woes, but it is demonstrably better than any alternative because it respects human dignity, resolves conflicts peacefully, and ensures rulers remain answerable to the governed.
